reasons: No tests are visible in this packet.
The docstrings describe several checks that were added after bugs, but their tests are not visible here.

terms.meaning: A class that defines which fields a result must contain and what type each field is.
Set so the object cannot be changed after it is created.
A check that runs when an object is created and refuses it if it is inconsistent.
A shared capability that is counted once, however many processes use it.
A range of values with a low, base and high figure.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Rounding and purpose of the outputs
sections.what: Sets the rounding to six decimal places and explains that all outputs are produced by arithmetic, not by an agent.
sections.why: The docstring says the same input must give byte-identical output, and rounding guards against small floating-point differences between runs.
sections.watch_out: Changing the rounding changes every number that is printed or stored.

sections.name: rounded
sections.title: Rounding a single number
sections.what: Rounds one number to the agreed precision.
sections.why: Same reason as the rounding setting: the output must not change between runs or platforms.
sections.watch_out: Values that are not passed through this function may differ slightly from those that are.

sections.name: rounded_range
sections.title: Rounding a range
sections.what: Rounds all three values of a range: low, base and high.
sections.why: Keeps each range rounded in the same way as single numbers.
sections.watch_out: It does not check that low is below high. That check is not made here.

sections.name: Assumption
sections.title: Named assumption
sections.what: Describes one named input with its value and where it came from. An empty evidence list means it is a stated assumption rather than a finding.
sections.why: The docstring says a figure must be defensible and updatable, which requires its assumptions to be listed.
sections.watch_out: The value and basis are text, so an assumption can be recorded without a real source.

sections.name: ProcessValue
sections.title: Value for one process
sections.what: Holds the full figures for one process: confidence, widening, whether it has evidence, effort before and after deduplication, the realised fraction, the in-horizon factor and the gross benefit.
sections.why: The field notes say the realised fraction already includes timing, so the in-horizon factor is only a diagnostic.
sections.watch_out: Multiplying the realised fraction by the in-horizon factor would count timing twice.

sections.name: EnablerPool
sections.title: Shared capability pool
sections.what: Describes one shared capability: who claims it, each claim, the pool counted once, the weights, the wave that delivers it and each claimant's credit.
sections.why: The docstring says a shared capability is counted once, using its largest single claim, and the built-in check enforces this.
sections.watch_out: The pool value must equal the largest claim. A sum would raise an error.

sections.name: WaveValue
sections.title: Wave summary
sections.what: Holds the results for one delivery wave: its start month, the processes in it, realised effort, gross money by currency and the share of its value that is evidenced.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the field descriptions.
sections.watch_out: The start month is a whole number. Its unit is only implied by its name, so check it before quoting.

sections.name: RunCostBreakdown
sections.title: Yearly run cost by currency
sections.what: Holds the yearly cost of running the estate in one currency, in five parts, and records whether inference was priced.
sections.why: The docstring says leaving out run cost is a common and serious omission in this kind of model.
sections.watch_out: The total adds the five parts. A new cost part must be added to that total as well.

sections.name: PrerequisiteCost
sections.title: Priced prerequisite
sections.what: Describes one prerequisite that must be built first: its build effort, its cost by currency, the wave that must deliver it and its evidence.
sections.why: The docstring says this closes a tracked issue, labelled D12 in the specification, where prerequisite work was being planned but not costed.
sections.watch_out: The wave is set to the wave before its earliest user, and never lower than the first wave.

sections.name: Bridge
sections.title: Bridge from gross to net
sections.what: Holds one currency's walk: gross benefit, prerequisite cost, implementation cost, run cost and net benefit, each as a range, plus a flag saying whether run cost was priced.
sections.why: The docstring says the flag is kept on the bridge so that a reader cannot mistake an unpriced estate for a cheap one.
sections.watch_out: If run cost is not priced, the net figure is too high. Any report that drops this flag misleads its reader.

sections.name: SensitivityResult
sections.title: Sensitivity for one driver
sections.what: Holds the net benefit at the low and high ends of one driver, and the gap between them.
sections.why: Used to rank the assumptions by how much they move the answer.
sections.watch_out: The gap is an absolute size, so it does not show direction. Read the low and high values for direction.

sections.name: BaselineTie
sections.title: Tie to one client's baseline
sections.what: Holds one client's net benefit, their stated revenue and earnings, the shares of each, and a flag for net above earnings.
sections.why: The docstring says an implausible result is flagged and never silently reduced.
sections.watch_out: A share is 0.0 when the baseline is zero, which can look like no impact.

sections.name: Reconciliation
sections.title: Reconciliation status
sections.what: Holds the status of the tie to client figures: either single client, or not summed across several clients, with the individual ties and a reason text.
sections.why: The docstring says the status should say what happened, instead of showing a total that implies a reconciliation that did not take place.
sections.watch_out: The reason text must be present exactly when the status is not single client. Both must be set together.

sections.name: PortfolioValue (part 1)
sections.title: Whole portfolio result, main fields
sections.what: Defines the complete output: depth tier, duplication ratio, evidenced share, effort totals, and the lists for processes, pools, waves, prerequisites, run costs, bridges, sensitivities, reconciliation and assumptions.
sections.why: The docstring says the three headline fields have no defaults, so a result cannot be built without them.
sections.watch_out: A caller that leaves out any required field gets an error by design.

sections.name: PortfolioValue: _check_ratio_is_consistent
sections.title: Consistency check on the ratio
sections.what: Checks that the duplication ratio equals gross effort divided by deduplicated effort within a tiny tolerance, and that a shared capability cannot appear beside a ratio of 1.0 or less.
sections.why: The docstring says the first check alone was not enough, because both totals came from the same calculation and a wrong dedupe could still pass it.
sections.watch_out: The second check is the important one. If it fails, the deduplication step did not remove any overlap.

summary: Defines the shapes of every output the value engine produces, and forces key figures to be present and consistent.
purpose: Holds the result objects that describe value per process, per wave, per shared capability, per currency and for the whole portfolio. It also checks that the totals agree with each other.
why: The docstring says the output must be the same every time it is run, and the three headline figures cannot be left out. Putting the checks in the shapes means a broken result cannot be built.
how: Step 1: fix the rounding precision. Step 2: define each result shape, such as process value, shared pool, wave, run cost, prerequisite cost, bridge, sensitivity, baseline tie and reconciliation. Step 3: run built-in checks when some shapes are created, for example that a shared pool equals its largest claim and that the reason is given exactly when the reconciliation is not single client. Step 4: the portfolio shape checks that the duplication ratio matches its two totals and that a shared capability cannot coexist with a ratio of 1.0 or less.
inputs: Numbers and lists produced by the calculation stages, along with the currency and identifiers they describe.
outputs: Validated result objects that the rendering and reporting code reads.
risks: Changing the rounding changes every emitted figure. The checks are strict, so a small change in a calculation stage may stop the whole run with an error. Most values are plain numbers with no unit label, so a mismatch in units would go unnoticed.
debug: If an error mentions a pool or ratio, read the message: it states the two numbers that disagree. If a value looks rounded oddly, check the rounding precision. If a new field is refused, check that the shape allows it.
